one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent consistently traded accuracy for model size by shrinking bucket and dimensionality across 148 steps instead of using fasttext post-training quantization (model.quantize), resulting in a final test accuracy of 0.5692 that never reached the required 0.62 threshold.
t_err_evidence: agent plans wrong fix: increase epochs, reduce dim/bucket instead of using more data or quantization
t_commit_evidence: At step 31, the second training run with reduced params (bucket=100k, dim=50, epoch=50, 100k samples) produced accuracy 0.5485 and size 102 MB. This confirmed the agent's capacity-reduction strategy was active and that no exploration of quantization or substantially more data would occur. From this point the agent iterated on minor parameter tweaks within the same flawed paradigm.
t_surface_evidence: Validation Precision: 0.5478... Model size: 102.37 MB; accuracy still below 0.62 threshold
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked knowledge of fasttext's post-training quantization API (model.quantize with qnorm=True and cutoff), which is the standard approach to reduce a large fasttext model's file size (from ~235 MB to <150 MB) without significantly impacting accuracy. Instead, it incorrectly tried to meet the size constraint by reducing architectural capacity (dim, bucket), which systematically harmed accuracy throughout the trajectory.
forewarning_evidence: Test Precision: 0.5692... Model size: 235.39 MB — both accuracy and size constraints violated
